findings.body: When `head` contains no space, the `None` branch returns `limit` characters of head plus the `…` character — `limit + 1` characters total — which exceeds the "at most `limit` characters" contract in the doc comment. A check-run title with no word boundary in the first `limit` characters (a long URL, a compound identifier) would be longer than the caller asked for and could exceed GitHub's own ceiling. No test covers this path: the Japanese fixture is only 16 characters so it short-circuits before truncation, and the `café` fixture always finds a space. The multibyte test asserts `chars().count() <= 21` for `limit = 20`, which accommodates the bug rather than catching it.
findings.title: Reserve one character for the ellipsis in shorten

value.summary: The PR adds a MongoDB kernel-bypass entrypoint, wires up embeddings config and auth env vars in compose, and introduces a `summarise` module with `shorten`/`first_sentence` helpers. The `shorten` function has an off-by-one: when the truncated head contains no space, it returns `limit + 1` characters (head + ellipsis), violating its own "at most `limit` characters" contract, and no test exercises that branch or pins the correct bound.
